utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Please be seated. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-74-A, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I would like to begin by ensuring that the audio equipment is working properly. Can the appellants hear the proceedings in a language they understand. Beginning with Mr. Prlic. Mr. Prlic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Stojic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Everything is all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything's fine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything fine here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything fine here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. May I -- I should point out that I think that Your Honour overlooked one of the accused, Mr. Coric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm terribly sorry. That's completely inexcusable and I beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: It was Mr. Coric, Mr. President, seated next to Mr. Pusic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Coric. I'm sorry. I misread --

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm really sorry. Next I would like the appearances by the Prosecution, so we are coming back to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Mr. President. For the Prosecution, Douglas Stringer, Katharine Marsden, and our case manager, Mr. Colin Nawrot.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stringer. For the Defence now. For Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Suzana Tomanovic, co-counsel for Dr. Jadranko Prlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Tomanovic. For Mr. Stojic, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Senka Nozica, counsel for Mr. Stojic, and Michelle Gonsalves and Brooke Stedman, Mr. Stojic's legal assistants.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Nozica. For Mr. Praljak. Mr. Praljak is representing himself.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Registrar, after your judgement by which you confirmed his allegations about my financial status, removed my two counsel, Ms. Nika Pinter and Ms. Natacha Fauveau-Ivanovic, from my case which is why I'm representing myself. Obviously, it is the Registrar's right to stop paying my counsel after your decision. However, I don't think that it is his right to remove them from my case because it has to do with the confidential relationship between myself and them. So they could have given in their notice to me or I could have removed them myself. Obviously they expressed their wish to deal with the procedural issues, and to make sure that I make the right decision on representing myself and that involves all the technical problems. They expressed their wish that I submitted to the Registrar in writing to defend me or, rather, to represent me pro bono for a certain while until we are able to deal with the technical problems. However, for the purposes of this particular session, I'm going to represent myself. Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Praljak. For Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. I'm Vesna Alaburic, and with my colleague Guenael Mettraux, we are counsel for Mr. Petkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Alaburic. For Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: MS. TOMASEGOVIC-TOMIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Representing Mr. Coric, Ms. Tomasegovic-Tomic, co-counsel Drazen Plavec, and legal counsel, Mr. Stephane Bourgon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Ms. Tomasegovic-Tomic. For Mr. Pusic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. Representing Mr. Pusic, counsel Ibrisimovic from Sarajevo and Mr. Mulalic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ibrisimovic. As you are aware, Rule 65 bis (B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence requires a status conference to be convened within 120 days after the filing of a Notice of Appeal, and thereafter, within 120 days after the last status conference for each appellant in the Tribunal's custody. A status conference serves two primary purposes. First, it allows the appellants an opportunity to express concerns relating to their appeal or detention conditions and for the Tribunal to inquire about the mental and physical condition of the detained persons. Second, it provides an opportunity to update the appellants with respect to the status of their case. In the present case, Notices of Appeal of Mr. Praljak and Mr. Pusic, were filed on 28 June 2013. Thus the status conference is taking place before the expiration of the 120-day period specified in Rule 65 bis (B). Today's status conference was scheduled by an order issued on 13 September 2013. I turn to the situation and health of the appellants, and I would like to begin by inquiring into the status conference -- of the detention conditions and health situation of the appellants. If you wish, if any one of the appellants wishes, I would close the session and have this in closed session. Anyone who would want me to close the session? I see no such request. Therefore I will proceed with an open session. So let me now go by -- one by one and ask whether there are any problems. Mr. Prlic.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I am fine so far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm glad to hear that. Mr. Praljak? Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything is fine, Your Honour. I have no problems at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I'm terribly sorry. Let me -- let me go back to Mr. Stojic --

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was Mr. Stojic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me go back to Mr. Stojic. I'm terribly sorry. Mr. Stojic, everything is fine, I take it, as you said.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT STOJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything fine, Your Honour. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now we are coming to Mr. Praljak.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I take it you have no problems, and I'm glad to hear that. Mr. Petkovic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PETKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, everything is fine, no problem at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Coric?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any objections to the accommodation in the Detention Unit. However, I would like to provide certain information about my health. As of recently, I have been on the -- monitoring for heart problems. I had an infection of lymph nodes and some other minor problems, but that would be all from me for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I hope you are satisfied with the treatment you are getting?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT CORIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The health care in Detention Unit takes place in two parts. One part is in the Detention Unit itself and the other in the hospital. I must say that there is a difference between the two, and I have some minor objections to the first stage of the treatment which takes place in the Detention Unit. However, there is nothing major to report and I'm sure that we will be able to find a solution to those minor problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm very glad to hear that. Mr. Pusic?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PUSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have any problem with the Detention Unit. I've been having problems with my health. We all have problems with the diet in the Detention Unit. We have been eating the same uniform food for years now, so we are forced to buy food for our own money. We are not here of our own will and the food that we are offered is really below any standards.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Counsel for Mr. Pusic, did I understand you wanted --

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I thought that Mr. Pusic would be telling you about his health condition. You know that we submitted an ex parte confidential submission on provisional release. However, since he did not raise that issue, there is no need for us to go into closed session and deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, Claudia, could you kindly report to the Registrar about the comments I heard about the quality of the food, and I would be grateful if the Registrar would look into that. So let me turn now to recent procedural history of the case, an update of the case. On 21 June 2013, upon the request of the parties, I ordered that the Notices of Appeal of Mr. Prlic, Mr. Stojic, Mr. Petkovic, and Mr. Coric be filed within 60 days of the issuance of the English translation of the trial judgement and that, without prejudice, the Notices of Appeal of the remaining parties may be filed within 90 days of the issuance of the trial judgement. The Notices of Appeal of Mr. Praljak and Mr. Pusic were filed on 28 June 2013. The Notice of Appeal of the Prosecution was filed on 27 August 2013. On 22 August 2013, I granted, in part, requests by Mr. Praljak and ancillary request by the Prosecution, for an extension of time for the filing of their appeal briefs and for leave to exceed word limits. I also granted the request by Mr. Pusic for an extension of time to file his appeal brief. I ordered Mr. Praljak, Mr. Pusic, and the Prosecution to file their appeal briefs no later than 135 days from the issuance of the official English translation of the trial judgement. As a result, there is a harmonised briefing schedule in place for all parties. By the same decision, I allowed Mr. Praljak to file an appeal brief totalling no more than 45.000 words, and the Prosecution to file a response thereto within the same word limit. I note that I received a complete set of filings pertaining to the motions filed by the Prosecution and Mr. Pusic concerning the latter's Notice of Appeal filed on 15 and 26 July 2013 respectively. A decision on these issues will be delivered in due course. On 3 October 2013, Mr. Praljak filed a public urgent motion with confidential annexes requesting a stay of proceedings until he receives the translation of various documents into a language he understands, which is B/C/S. The Appeals Chamber has not yet received a response from the Prosecution to this request, as of this morning. On 4 October 2013, Mr. Praljak filed a public motion with public and confidential annexes requesting the assignment of his formerly Tribunal-paid counsel under the Tribunal's legal aid provisions which apply to level 3 cases. No response from the Prosecution has been filed yet. The Appeals Chamber will deal with Praljak's request of 3 and 4 October as soon as it has received responses in these matters. At this point, I would like to ask the parties whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Meron, on the 29th of August, 2013, I sent you a letter in which I asked from you, Your Honour, Judge Meron, and from Mr. Meron, I asked to reconsider the decision on my financial status. We are dealing with two things here. First of all, I've not received a reply yet, and that problem has been dragging on since 2005, i.e. for the full eight years. Throughout the eight years --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Can I ask you just to kindly stop for one second? Let me tell you -- was it yesterday or this morning? Yesterday we filed an answer to you. It's already in the -- it has been formally filed. As regards the timing of this reply, you will have to read it and you will see whether you still have problems after that. But it's all done. On the 7th of October, there is a decision called "Decision on Slobodan Praljak's request for further review."

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, if you have reached a decision, there is nothing further I can say before I read it. I would like to say that during the eight-year period, nobody has ever spoken to me. I don't know whether you're fully informed or not. None of my answers, none of the facts that I provided, have been either translated or have reached you, Your Honour, Judge Meron. I have provided a number of responses and there is one that I wrote on 103 pages, and I publicly claim here in public session that the Registry is running a complot against me, something that is not legally founded which is not part of any civilisation behaviour. This is a witchcraft that started a long time ago. Nobody ever checked anything. Nobody ever talked to me. There is no control mechanism that would allow anybody to investigate things. All the documents and facts are proclaimed either confidential or ex parte. I wanted that to be removed. However, even if this is not removed, I'm sure that in defending my dignity and in defending the truth, I'm going to publicise all that urbi et orbi. And now, Your Honour, Judge Meron, I would like to ask you just one more thing. Despite the fact that you sent me an answer, the letter that I sent you was translated into English almost well enough but not perfectly well, because there are some stylistic characteristics that have not been taken into account. I would kindly ask your staff to make a photocopy of a better translation for this to be provided to you, with your permission, of course, because this document is a better translation of the letter that I sent to you with my request in it, and the request was for the other side in the proceedings, and the other side is Slobodan Praljak in this case, to be heard, and to be able to present his own facts, his own claims, and to be able to show documents to bear witness to the facts that he is presenting. Thank you very much. Further on, there is one more thing that I would like to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Let me just ask the Registry to have a look at the accuracy of the translation, if there is something inaccurate, to advise me accordingly. Yes. Yes, and you can take into account the letter. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In a letter that was sent before the first instance decision was read, I requested from the Trial Chamber Judges, and from His Honour Judge Antonetti, to finally define the term of freedom or liberty when one is provisionally released for humanitarian reasons, and then he sent me a confidential reply in which he provided his opinion on that. And since that was done ex parte, only I and my counsel can actually read it and use it. However, since the position of His Honour Judge Antonetti on what is the definition of provisional release, as opposed to detention, and that differs from the customary positions of this Tribunal that had been voiced until then, and since this applies to all --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I am having some difficulty in discussing the propriety of correspondence between you and Judge Antonetti. That stage is gone, and especially if those things were ex parte, I would suggest that -- sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Sorry. I think that would be better not for you to proceed and you will see that in the decision which I issued yesterday on the 7th of October, there is something relevant to it. So why don't you just wait and read it.

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT PRALJAK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, in that case, I will wait before I can offer any further comments. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Praljak. Are there any other issues that any of the other appellants would like to raise? I see the Prosecution is --

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, nothing from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since there are no other matters being raised, I thank the parties for their attendance. I will adjourn the proceedings. Thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
